doc_friction.issue: `queue --severity high` listed research/swe-cachecost defects 0-1 as open with no fixed_by, but by the time mark-fixed ran on a fresh origin/main checkout they were already marked (another session landed it). The queue reads the local tree, so a stale checkout shows already-fixed rows.
--for-changes took about 25 minutes for a 6-file venture change plus a post, and the security-gate steps reached no verdict because the PyYAML hash-locked install fails in the cloud container.

I searched open PRs for 'ci-minutes' in:title before opening #19007 and found none. A parallel quality-fix session opened and merged #19008 on the same audit row minutes later. The queue's 'open PR naming it' marker can't see a PR that hasn't been opened yet, so two fix sessions that start together can take the same row. Claiming the row on a branch (like security_next.py --claim) would close that race.

Red on main after PRs #19013 and #19010 merged minutes apart. #19013's queue test used research/ subjects, and #19010 made queue drop paused research by default, so changed-ventures failed for every PR. Fixed here by switching the test's subjects to ventures/.

human_equivalent.basis: check four vendor pricing pages, update the rate card and tests, write a short post

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
